nodes.description: The Ant1-null mouse develops lactic acidosis, mitochondrial myopathy with mitochondrial proliferation, increased ROS and mtDNA damage, and a cardiomyopathy that is concentric but dilated. Extraocular muscle shows mitochondrial myopathy without ocular motor deficit, attributed to higher Ant2 expression there.

Combining Ant1 loss with a mild mtDNA ND6 variant worsens cardiomyopathy, modelling the haplogroup effect seen in patients; neonatal AAV delivery of Ant1 to these hearts ameliorated the cardiomyopathy.

nodes.description: Recessive SLC25A4 alleles remove ANT1 function. The homozygous p.Ala123Asp missense allele gives no measurable ATP uptake in proteoliposomes reconstituted from patient muscle; the homozygous c.111+1G>A splice-donor allele leaves no detectable ANT1 transcript in muscle or fibroblasts; and the Mennonite founder frameshift c.523delC is a null allele. In a bacterial expression assay the recessive missense alleles retained less than 1% of wild-type transport, lower than either the adPEO or the de novo dominant alleles, even though the recessive disease is clinically milder than the de novo disorder. One compound heterozygous patient (p.Arg236Pro with a frameshift) with a milder course is thought to retain some functional protein.

nodes.description: Coupled mitochondrial energy supply to the cytosol fails in the striated muscles that depend on ANT1. Unlike a primary respiratory chain defect, the respiratory chain enzymes themselves are increased in patient muscle, so the deficit lies in delivering mitochondrial ATP rather than in making it. In patient fibroblasts (which express little ANT1) basal respiration and ATP production were reduced, though not significantly in a small sample; in ANT1-deficient mouse muscle exercise stalls the TCA cycle through NAD+ limitation.
